# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 20, 2026
**Re:** Vaibur Water Services, LLC / Taipux Chemical Corp.: review of supply documentation and key issues for the client

---

## 1. Summary

We reviewed all ten documents in the folder:

- Supply Agreement
- Order Form No. 1
- Quality Agreement
- Parent Guaranty
- Amendment No. 1
- Supply Continuity Side Letter
- Data Processing Addendum
- Price Adjustment Notice
- Insurance Certificate Cover Letter
- Term Sheet

The Supply Agreement is governed by Delaware law and took effect on **March 1, 2024** (the Effective Date, Supply Agreement §2.1).

Four issues need the client's attention. Each one comes from reading two or more documents together:

| # | Issue | Main location | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Exclusivity covers all treatment chemicals at every U.S. facility. The term sheet agreed coagulants at six plants only. | Supply Agreement §3.1 (with §1.9) | High. Vaibur may already be in breach. |
| 2 | Automatic renewal for successive **seven-year** terms, with a **180-day** notice window | Amendment No. 1 §§2 and 3 | High. This is a long-term lock-in. |
| 3 | Vaibur's environmental indemnity for releases at its own plants is **uncapped** | Supply Agreement §11.3(a) (with §1.4) and Quality Agreement §8.2 | High. Exposure is unlimited. |
| 4 | Taipux can assign the whole agreement without consent to unaffiliated third parties that it adds by notice | Supply Agreement §15.2 (with §1.12) and Side Letter §2 | Medium–High |

**Order of precedence.** Supply Agreement §1.6 sets the order in which the documents prevail if they conflict:

1. amendments and side letters;
2. the Supply Agreement;
3. the Quality Agreement;
4. Order Forms.

So **amendments and side letters prevail over the Supply Agreement**. This drives Issues 2 and 4.

"This Agreement" is defined in §1.4 to include the Quality Agreement, Order Forms, amendments and side letters. This drives Issue 3.

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: Overbroad exclusivity

**Location**
- Supply Agreement §3.1 (Exclusive Purchase), read with §1.9 (definition of "Treatment Chemicals").
- Compare Term Sheet §3.3.

**What the documents say**
- Section 3.1 requires Vaibur to buy "100% of its requirements of **all Treatment Chemicals** exclusively from Supplier."
- This applies "for every facility **owned, operated or managed** by Customer or its Affiliates in the United States."
- Vaibur must also cause its Affiliates not to buy elsewhere.
- Section 1.9 defines Treatment Chemicals as *all* water and wastewater treatment chemicals. This expressly includes disinfectants, oxidants, pH/alkalinity chemicals, corrosion inhibitors, dechlorination agents, odor control chemicals and sludge conditioning chemicals.
- The Term Sheet (§3.3) recorded a much narrower deal: exclusivity "for ferric chloride and polyaluminum chloride coagulants for the six Listed Plants only." It stated that Vaibur "remains free to buy all other chemicals, and to buy any chemicals for any other plant or facility, from any supplier."
- Term Sheet §3.4 confirmed that adding products or plants would not extend exclusivity without express written agreement.
- Order Form No. 1 covers only ferric chloride and PACl at the six Listed Plants.

**Why it matters to the client**
- **Possible current breach.** As drafted, Vaibur is barred from buying chlorine, hypochlorite, caustic, lime, polymers and every other chemical from anyone except Taipux, at every U.S. plant. Taipux currently sells only two coagulants. Vaibur almost certainly buys these other chemicals elsewhere today, so it is likely in technical breach. That gives Taipux:
  - a termination threat under §12.1 (30-day cure for material breach);
  - a damages claim; and
  - negotiating leverage.
- **Managed facilities.** The clause covers facilities Vaibur only *manages* for municipal owners. Many of those O&M contracts require the municipality's own procurement or competitive bidding. Vaibur could be caught between its contract with the municipality and this exclusivity.
- **Affiliates and acquisitions.** The clause binds Affiliates and future facilities. Any acquisition or new O&M contract is swept in automatically.
- **Duration.** The exclusivity now runs for a seven-year initial term with seven-year renewals (Issue 2).
- **Only exit routes.** The only relief is temporary: §14.2 (force majeure, for affected Products only) and §4.4 (shortfall cover).
- **The Term Sheet will not fix this on its own.** It is expressly non-binding (Term Sheet §15.1). Under Term Sheet §1.3, Vaibur's own counsel prepared the first draft. That weakens any mistake or reformation argument.
- **Some help for Vaibur.** The Supply Agreement has no entire-agreement clause. The Term Sheet, the Order Form and Amendment No. 1 Recital B (tanks for coagulants only) are good evidence of the parties' common understanding. That supports a negotiated correction.

**Recommended fix**
1. **Amend §3.1** to the agreed scope: exclusivity only for ferric chloride and polyaluminum chloride, and only for the Listed Plants in Schedule 1 to Order Form No. 1. State expressly that:
   - Vaibur may buy all other chemicals, and any chemicals for any other facility, from any supplier; and
   - adding Products or Customer Sites does not extend exclusivity unless expressly agreed in writing (mirroring Term Sheet §3.4).
2. **Carve out** facilities that Vaibur manages for third-party owners, and any facility where the owner or an applicable law or procurement rule requires another supplier.
3. **Obtain a waiver and release now** from Taipux of any past non-compliance with §3.1 as drafted. This can go in the same amendment.
4. **Practical step.** Until the amendment is signed, find out internally what Vaibur buys from other suppliers, and at which sites, so we understand the exposure. The client should not raise the point with Taipux informally before we have a strategy.

---

### Issue 2: Automatic renewal for successive seven-year terms

**Location**
- Amendment No. 1 (dated June 15, 2025): §2 (replacing Supply Agreement §2.1) and §3 (replacing Supply Agreement §2.2).

**What the documents say**
- **Original terms (now superseded).** As originally signed, the Supply Agreement had:
  - a three-year Initial Term;
  - one-year Renewal Terms; and
  - a 90-day non-renewal notice period.

  This matched Term Sheet §4.
- **Amendment No. 1 §2** extends the Initial Term to "**seven (7) years**" from March 1, 2024. The Initial Term therefore now runs to **March 1, 2031**.
- **Amendment No. 1 §3** replaces the renewal clause. The agreement now renews automatically for successive Renewal Terms "**equal in length to the Initial Term**," which means seven years each. Renewal is avoided only if notice is given "at least **one hundred eighty (180) days** before the end of the then-current term."
- Under §1.6, amendments prevail over the Supply Agreement. The original one-year renewal and 90-day notice period **no longer apply**.
- The stated rationale (Recital C) is Taipux's need to amortize the bulk storage tanks. That rationale supports a longer *initial* term. It does not support seven-year *renewals*.

**Why it matters to the client**
- **One missed deadline means seven more years.** If Vaibur misses the notice window, it is locked in until 2038. The overbroad exclusivity (Issue 1) and the uncapped indemnity (Issue 3) come with it.
- **The window is long and early.** Notice must be given about six months before expiry. The non-renewal notice deadline for the Initial Term falls on or about **September 2, 2030**: 180 days before March 1, 2031. We should confirm whether "seven years from the Effective Date" ends on February 28 or March 1, 2031.
- **Limited exits during the term.** Vaibur has no termination-for-convenience right. Its exits are limited to:
  - breach (§12.1);
  - insolvency (§12.2);
  - supply failure (§12.3); and
  - prolonged force majeure (§14.3).
- **Costly exit on renewal.** Prices can rise once a year under §6.3 (as the December 2025 notice shows). Vaibur's only real price discipline is the threat of non-renewal, and that threat is now expensive to use.

**Recommended fix**
1. **Negotiate an amendment** so that Renewal Terms are **one year** each and the non-renewal notice period goes back to **90 days**. This matches the Term Sheet and the original bargain.
2. **Fallback options:**
   - a right for Vaibur to terminate for convenience at any time during a Renewal Term, on 90–180 days' notice; or
   - a right to terminate early in the Initial Term, with Vaibur paying Taipux's documented unamortized tank cost (Amendment §4). This answers Taipux's stated amortization concern directly.
3. **Leverage.** The seven-year Initial Term was given in exchange for the tanks. Seven-year *renewals* go beyond that rationale. Taipux should be asked to justify them.
4. **Calendar now.** Docket the non-renewal deadline (on or before **September 2, 2030**) with multiple reminders, starting no later than early 2030. Re-docket for each Renewal Term.
5. **Housekeeping.** Confirm that the Parent Guaranty acknowledgment required by Amendment §5.2 (due within ten Business Days after June 15, 2025) was actually delivered. It is not in the folder.

---

### Issue 3: Vaibur's environmental indemnity is uncapped

**Location**
- Supply Agreement §11.3(a), read with §1.4 (definition of "this Agreement") and §11.1 (cap).
- Quality Agreement §8.2 (Customer Indemnity).

**What the documents say**
- **The cap.** Section 11.1 caps each party's liability at the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.
- **The carve-out.** Section 11.3(a) removes from the cap, and from the consequential damages exclusion, "**any Environmental Claim indemnity obligation** of *either Party* under this Agreement."
- **Looked at alone, the carve-out favours Vaibur.** Within the Supply Agreement itself, the only Environmental Claim indemnity is **Taipux's** (§10.2).
- **Why it does not, read with §1.4.** Section 1.4 defines "this Agreement" to include the **Quality Agreement**.
- **Vaibur's own indemnity.** Quality Agreement §8.2 provides that "**Customer shall indemnify**, defend and hold harmless Supplier, its Affiliates and their respective officers, employees and agents" against any Environmental Claim "arising from any release, spill or discharge of Products **after delivery at Customer Sites**."
- **Result.** Read together, Vaibur's §8.2 indemnity is an Environmental Claim indemnity under "this Agreement." It therefore falls within the §11.3(a) carve-out and is **uncapped**. It is also not protected by the exclusion of consequential damages.
- **Precedence does not help.** The two documents do not conflict, so §1.6 does not apply.
- **Survival.** Quality Agreement §11.1 makes §8.2 survive termination for as long as any delivered Product remains in Vaibur's possession.

**Why it matters to the client**
- **Unlimited exposure at Vaibur's own plants.** The indemnity covers CERCLA, RCRA, Clean Water Act and similar liabilities for any release of ferric chloride or PACl, which are corrosive and acidic. This includes:
  - cleanup;
  - natural resource damages;
  - fines and penalties; and
  - third-party bodily injury and property damage.

  Vaibur stores, handles and feeds these chemicals daily, so this is the most likely route to an environmental claim.
- **The indemnity is not fault-based.** It applies to "any" release after delivery, even one caused by Taipux's tank failure. This matters especially because Taipux owns and maintains the on-site Tanks under Amendment §4.4.
- **Overlap with Taipux's indemnity.** Delivery is DAP, which occurs on arrival. But title and risk pass only on completion of offloading (§5.2), and Taipux's §10.2(a) indemnity runs until then. A spill during offloading could therefore fall under *both* indemnities. Taipux would argue Vaibur's uncapped indemnity applies.
- **No basis in the deal terms.** The Term Sheet (§10.2) contemplated a mutual cap with only "customary" exclusions. A one-way, uncapped customer environmental indemnity is not customary.

**Recommended fix**
1. **Narrow §11.3(a)** so that it applies only to "Supplier's obligations under Section 10.2."
2. **Alternatively, cap Vaibur's indemnity expressly.** Amend Quality Agreement §8.2 to state that it is subject to Supply Agreement §11.1 and §11.2 "notwithstanding Section 11.3(a)."
3. **Make §8.2 fault-based.** Limit it to releases "to the extent caused by the negligence or breach of Customer," and exclude releases caused by:
   - Supplier, its carriers or contractors;
   - the Tanks; or
   - non-conforming Product.
4. **Align the trigger with Taipux's indemnity.** Change "after delivery" to "after title and risk pass under Section 5.2," so the two indemnities meet at the same point with no overlap.
5. **Interim step.** Ask the client to confirm that its own pollution and environmental liability insurance responds to contractual indemnities of this kind.

---

### Issue 4: Unrestricted assignment by Taipux to third parties

**Location**
- Supply Agreement §15.2 (Permitted Assignment), read with §1.12 (definition of "Supplier Group").
- Side Letter dated October 7, 2024, §2.1 and Annex 1.

**What the documents say**
- **The assignment right.** Section 15.2 lets Taipux assign the agreement, in whole or in part, "without Customer's consent to **any member of the Supplier Group**." Taipux need only give notice within ten Business Days after the assignment.
- **Looked at alone, this is routine.** Section 1.12 defines Supplier Group as Taipux and its Affiliates, which is an ordinary affiliate carve-out.
- **The Side Letter widens it.** The Side Letter was signed after the Gulfport outage to broaden backup sourcing under §4.3. But §2.1 provides that, "**for purposes of the Agreement**," Supplier Group also includes "the **contract manufacturers and distributors** listed in Annex 1, **as Supplier may update** Annex 1 from time to time by written notice."
- **The Side Letter controls.** Under §1.6, side letters prevail over the Supply Agreement, so the expanded definition governs. It is not limited to §4.3.

**Why it matters to the client**
- **Assignment to unknown third parties.** Taipux can assign the entire agreement to any of the six unaffiliated Annex 1 companies without Vaibur's consent. It can also assign to *anyone else it adds to Annex 1 by unilateral notice*, potentially including a distributor aligned with a Vaibur competitor. The assigned rights would include the exclusivity, Vaibur's uncapped indemnity and confidential plant data.
- **Vaibur gets no say in its counterparty.** It could end up locked into exclusive supply, for seven-year terms, with an unvetted company.
- **Credit support could fall away.** The Parent Guaranty covers the obligations of "the Supplier," Taipux Chemical Corp. (Guaranty §1.3 and Recital B). Once the agreement is assigned to a third party, that party's performance is not covered by the Guaranty. Guaranty §3.2(a) preserves the Guaranty through amendments, but it does not clearly reach an unaffiliated assignee's obligations.
- **Confidential information.** Supply Agreement §13 information (pricing, volumes, plant operating data) would pass to the assignee.
- **Inconsistent with the Term Sheet.** Term Sheet §13 contemplated assignment only with consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, with only *affiliate* assignment left open.

**Recommended fix**
1. **Amend Side Letter §2.1** so that the expanded definition applies "solely for purposes of Section 4.3 of the Supply Agreement (Alternate Sourcing)" and "not for purposes of Section 15 or any other provision."
2. **Alternatively, amend §15.2** to:
   - define Supplier Group "as defined in Section 1.12, without regard to any side letter"; and
   - require Vaibur's prior written consent for any assignment to a person that is not an Affiliate of Supplier.
3. **Protect the Guaranty.** Require that any permitted assignment is conditional on Taipux Holdings, Inc. confirming in writing that the Guaranty extends to the assignee's obligations. Alternatively, Taipux should remain jointly liable after assignment.
4. **Control Annex 1 additions.** Give Vaibur a right to object to new Annex 1 entries, for example competitors or entities that fail quality or credit checks, within a short period after notice.

---

## 3. Other documents reviewed: no material issues

- **Order Form No. 1:** consistent with the Term Sheet on products, plants, prices, lead times and net 45 payment terms. No issues.
- **Parent Guaranty:** broad guaranty of payment and performance with a continuing guaranty and appropriate waivers. The only concern is the assignee gap noted in Issue 4. Confirm that the Amendment §5.2 acknowledgment was received.
- **Price Adjustment Notice (December 15, 2025):**
  - It appears compliant with §6.3. It is the only adjustment in the period beginning March 1, 2025, gives more than 60 days' notice (effective February 16, 2026), and attaches supporting documentation.
  - The Annex A arithmetic checks: +5.0% for ferric chloride and +4.0% for PACl.
  - The client may still request a §6.3 review meeting to test the underlying invoices.
- **Data Processing Addendum:** a standard independent-controller arrangement for limited business contact and driver data, with liability subject to §11. No issues.
- **Insurance Certificate Cover Letter (February 20, 2026):** the renewed limits, insurer ratings and additional-insured status meet the §9.1 and §9.2 minimums. The client should simply obtain and file the enclosed endorsements.

---

## 4. Recommended next steps

1. **Internal compliance check on exclusivity.** Before approaching Taipux, confirm with the client what chemicals it buys from other suppliers, and for which facilities.
2. **Single amendment package.** Prepare one Amendment No. 2 and Side Letter amendment covering:
   - exclusivity narrowed to the agreed scope, plus a waiver of past non-compliance;
   - one-year renewals and a 90-day notice period, or a termination right;
   - the §11.3(a) carve-out limited to Taipux's §10.2 indemnity, and a capped, fault-based §8.2;
   - the Supplier Group expansion confined to §4.3, and consent required for non-affiliate assignment.
3. **Leverage.** Use the Term Sheet as the anchor. Each fix restores the agreed deal rather than seeking new concessions.
4. **Docket deadlines.** Diary the non-renewal deadline (on or before September 2, 2030), the annual price-adjustment windows and the annual Guaranty financial statement deliveries (Guaranty §6.1).

Please let me know if you would like me to draft the amendment language or a short client-facing summary.

# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 20, 2026
**Re:** Vaibur Water Services, LLC – Review of Taipux Chemical Corp. supply documents

---

## 1. Summary

We act for Vaibur Water Services, LLC ("Vaibur") in its chemical supply relationship with Taipux Chemical Corp. ("Taipux"). Taipux Holdings, Inc. ("Holdings") guarantees Taipux's obligations. I reviewed all ten documents in the folder:

1. Supply Agreement
2. Order Form No. 1
3. Quality Agreement
4. Parent Guaranty
5. Amendment No. 1
6. Supply Continuity Side Letter
7. Data Processing Addendum
8. Price Adjustment Notice
9. Insurance Certificate Cover Letter
10. Term Sheet

The Supply Agreement is governed by Delaware law. It took effect on **March 1, 2024** (the "Effective Date") under Supply Agreement § 2.1.

Three issues need the client's attention. In order of priority:

1. **Auto-renewal (Amendment No. 1 §§ 2–3).** The agreement now renews automatically for successive **seven-year** terms unless notice is given at least **180 days** before expiry.
2. **Uncapped indemnity (Supply Agreement § 11.3 with Quality Agreement § 8.2).** Vaibur's environmental indemnity for post-delivery releases at its own plants falls outside the liability cap and is therefore **unlimited**.
3. **Assignment (Supply Agreement § 15.2 with Side Letter § 2).** Taipux can assign the agreement **without consent** to unaffiliated contract manufacturers and distributors that it can add unilaterally. This could include a Vaibur competitor.

**Order of precedence.** One structural point affects two of these issues. Under Supply Agreement § 1.6, if the documents conflict, they prevail in this order:

1. amendments and side letters;
2. the Supply Agreement;
3. the Quality Agreement;
4. Order Forms.

So **amendments and side letters prevail over the Supply Agreement**. Section 1.4 also defines "this Agreement" to include the Quality Agreement, the Order Forms, and every amendment and side letter. Several provisions therefore have to be read together, not document by document.

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1 – Seven-year automatic renewal

**Location:** Amendment No. 1 (dated June 15, 2025), Sections 2 and 3. These replace Supply Agreement §§ 2.1 and 2.2.

**What it says:**
- **Section 2** replaces the Initial Term with "seven (7) years" from the March 1, 2024 Effective Date. The Initial Term now runs to **March 1, 2031**.
- **Section 3** replaces § 2.2. The agreement now renews automatically for successive Renewal Terms "equal in length to the Initial Term", which means seven years each. Renewal is avoided only by written notice of non-renewal given at least "one hundred eighty (180) days" before the end of the then-current term.
- Amendments prevail over the Supply Agreement under § 1.6. The original terms no longer apply: one-year renewals and a 90-day notice period. Those terms also reflected the deal in Term Sheet § 4.

**Why it matters:**
- The recital says Taipux needed a longer term to amortize the bulk storage tanks it is installing at four Listed Plants. That commercial reason supports a longer *initial* term. It does not explain why every *renewal* should also be seven years.
- In practice, one missed notice window commits Vaibur to a further seven years: to March 2038, and then to 2045.
- Vaibur has limited exit rights. It can terminate only for breach (§ 12.1), insolvency (§ 12.2), supply failure (§ 12.3) or prolonged force majeure (§ 14.3). It has no termination for convenience.
- During that time, Taipux can still raise prices once a year under § 6.3.
- The 180-day window is long and easy to miss. If the Initial Term ends on March 1, 2031, non-renewal notice must be received by about **October 31, 2030**. We should confirm the exact date against the drafting. Notice must be given under § 16.4, and it is effective on receipt.
- Also note a point of caution. Under the original terms, the first non-renewal deadline would have fallen around early December 2026, which is next month. That deadline is **no longer relevant** because of the amendment. Nobody at the client should rely on the old 90-day / one-year mechanism.

**Recommended fix:**
- Propose Amendment No. 2. It should:
  - restore **one-year Renewal Terms**, keeping the seven-year Initial Term if the tank investment justifies it; and
  - reduce the notice period to **90 days**.
- Alternatively, seek a right for Vaibur to terminate for convenience during any Renewal Term on, say, 90–180 days' notice. Pair this with a pro-rata unamortized tank buy-out or removal mechanism, building on Amendment § 4.5.
- If Taipux resists, cap the number of renewals or limit Renewal Terms to two or three years.
- **Immediate step:** diarize the non-renewal deadline (about October 31, 2030) with reminders at 12, 9 and 7 months beforehand. Record it in the client's contract management system.
- Confirm that Holdings delivered the guaranty acknowledgment required by Amendment § 5.2 within ten Business Days after June 15, 2025. Parent Guaranty § 3.2(a) probably makes this belt-and-braces, but the acknowledgment should be on file.

---

### Issue 2 – Vaibur's environmental indemnity is uncapped

**Location:** Supply Agreement § 11.3(a), read with § 1.4 and Quality Agreement § 8.2.

**What it says:**
- Supply Agreement § 11.1 caps each party's liability at the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim. Section 11.2 excludes consequential damages.
- Section 11.3(a) removes both protections for "any Environmental Claim indemnity obligation of either Party under this Agreement".
- Within the Supply Agreement itself, the only environmental indemnity is Taipux's indemnity in § 10.2. That one covers releases before title passes and non-conforming product. Read alone, the carve-out therefore looks favourable to Vaibur.
- However, "this Agreement" includes the Quality Agreement under § 1.4, and Quality Agreement § 1.2 confirms this.
- Quality Agreement § 8.2 provides that "Customer shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless" Taipux, its Affiliates and their personnel against any Environmental Claim "arising from any release, spill or discharge of Products after delivery at Customer Sites."
- That is an Environmental Claim indemnity under "this Agreement". It therefore falls within § 11.3(a).
- Precedence does not help, because the documents do not conflict. They operate together.

**Why it matters:**
- Vaibur's exposure for any chemical release at its own plants after delivery is **unlimited and includes consequential loss**. This covers spills from storage tanks, feed systems or secondary containment.
- "Environmental Claim" (§ 1.3) is very broad. It covers fines, penalties, remediation, natural resource damages, personal injury and property damage under the Clean Water Act, the Safe Drinking Water Act, CERCLA, RCRA and state equivalents.
- Ferric chloride and PACl are corrosive, acidic products, and Vaibur stores them in bulk. Taipux-owned Tanks are being installed at four plants under Amendment § 4. Vaibur provides the pads and secondary containment for those Tanks (§ 4.3).
- The indemnity is not limited to releases caused by Vaibur's negligence. It is drafted on an "arising from" basis. On its face, it could catch a release caused partly by a defect in Taipux's own Tank.
- The indemnity survives termination under Quality Agreement § 11.1 for as long as any delivered Product remains in Vaibur's possession.
- The term sheet (§ 10.2) contemplated a mutual 12-month-fees cap, subject only to "customary" exclusions. An uncapped customer handling indemnity is not customary.

**Recommended fix (in order of preference):**
1. Amend Supply Agreement § 11.3(a) to read: "Supplier's indemnity obligations under Section 10.2." This confines the carve-out to Taipux's environmental indemnity.
2. Alternatively, amend Quality Agreement § 8.2 to state expressly that Vaibur's indemnity is subject to §§ 11.1 and 11.2. Also limit it "to the extent" the claim is caused by Customer's negligence or breach of Quality Agreement § 8.1. Expressly exclude releases caused by Products' non-conformity, by Supplier's carriers during offloading, or by the Tanks or Supplier's maintenance of them.
3. In any event, ask the client's risk team to confirm that Vaibur's own pollution liability cover responds to contractual indemnities of this kind.

---

### Issue 3 – Taipux can assign to unaffiliated third parties without consent

**Location:** Supply Agreement § 15.2 (with § 1.12), read with Side Letter (October 7, 2024) § 2 and Annex 1.

**What it says:**
- Section 15.1 requires consent for assignment, which may not be unreasonably withheld.
- Section 15.2 lets Taipux assign the agreement "in whole or in part, without Customer's consent to any member of the Supplier Group". It only has to give notice within ten Business Days after the assignment takes effect.
- Section 1.12 defines Supplier Group as Taipux and its Affiliates. On its own, that is a routine affiliate carve-out.
- Side Letter § 2.1 then provides that, "for purposes of the Agreement", Supplier Group also includes the "contract manufacturers and distributors" listed in Annex 1, "as Supplier may update Annex 1 from time to time by written notice".
- The Side Letter was negotiated to secure backup sourcing under § 4.3 after the Gulfport outage. However, the definition is not limited to § 4.3.
- Side letters prevail over the Supply Agreement under § 1.6. The expanded definition therefore also flows into § 15.2.

**Why it matters:**
- Taipux can transfer the whole agreement to any of the six unaffiliated companies in Annex 1. It can also add any other contract manufacturer or distributor by notice and then assign to that company, all without Vaibur's consent. Three of the six are distributors.
- An assignee could be a company Vaibur has never vetted, or a competitor of Vaibur in water services. That assignee would gain access to Vaibur's pricing, volumes and plant operating data, which are Confidential Information under § 13.1.
- Credit support could be lost. The Parent Guaranty secures obligations of "the Supplier" (Taipux Chemical Corp.). Once the agreement is assigned to an unaffiliated third party, it is doubtful that Holdings would remain on the hook for the assignee's performance. Vaibur could end up with an unguaranteed counterparty for the rest of a seven-year (or longer) term.
- This departs from Term Sheet § 13. That section required consent, with only *affiliate* assignment left to be addressed.
- A related point: under Side Letter § 3.3, supply from an Annex 1 source for up to 60 consecutive days is not a manufacturing-site change needing Quality Agreement § 5.2 approval. That is acceptable for emergencies. But it confirms that Vaibur has no approval right over additions to Annex 1.

**Recommended fix:**
- Amend Side Letter § 2.1 so that the expanded Supplier Group applies **"solely for purposes of Section 4.3 (Alternate Sourcing) of the Supply Agreement"**. State expressly that it does not apply to § 15.2 or any other provision.
- Give Vaibur a right to object to additions to Annex 1, for example on competitor or quality grounds.
- Alternatively, amend § 15.2 to permit consent-free assignment only to Affiliates "as defined in Section 1.12 without regard to any side letter". The assignment should also be conditional on:
  - Holdings confirming in writing that the Parent Guaranty continues to apply to the assignee; and
  - the assignee not being a competitor of Vaibur.
- Also consider changing notice of assignment from after the event to at least 30 days in advance.

---

## 3. Other documents – no material issues

- **Order Form No. 1.** This is consistent with the Term Sheet: six Listed Plants, ferric chloride and PACl, the agreed prices, and net 45-day payment (§ 7.2, matching Supply Agreement § 6.2). There are no issues.
- **Parent Guaranty.** It is broad: a guaranty of payment and performance covering the Quality Agreement and Order Forms, and it survives amendments (§ 3.2(a)). See Issue 3 on the risk that it does not follow an assignee. Minor drafting point: § 7.2 ties Vaibur's right to assign the Guaranty to an assignment "in accordance with Section 15.2". That works, but it should be checked if § 15.2 is redrafted.
- **Price Adjustment Notice (December 15, 2025).** This appears compliant with § 6.3:
  - it is the first adjustment in the period beginning March 1, 2025;
  - it gives more than 60 days' notice (effective February 16, 2026);
  - it is limited to raw material, energy and freight costs; and
  - it encloses supporting documentation.
